new_text.add_article_media: Add a screenshot or GIF to the article. It goes right after the block holding the screenshot named in `after` ("start" for the top), in place of the screenshot named in `replace`, or else at the end of the article. Returns its screenshot_id (it appears in the article as `<SCREENSHOT screenshot_id>`)

- kind="blank": empty slide clips you'll populate with add_elements / generate_media. Pass `clips: [{title?, duration?}, ...]`. Note: create_project already creates clip 0; calling with N blank entries gives N+1 clips total.
- kind="pptx": extr
new_text.add_elements:
Add elements to one or more clips in ONE call (always batch). Items apply in order; one result per item (partial success ok). type_data shape: get_element_schema.

- `defaults`: hoist what repeats (clip_index, element_type, font_setting, alignment…); items carry only what differs. `returning` shapes

Insert one sync marker on a clip's transcript.

- The user is explicit about WHERE the camera should pause / cut (e.g. "sync the word 'submit' to 4.2s of the demo").
- `auto_sync` ran but missed a step you care about.

How matching works:
- `word`: case-insensitive; punctuation and ap

Run the agentic auto-sync pipeline on a clip with a source recording: detects natural sync points (UI changes, narrated steps) and inserts sync-marker nodes into its transcript. Required before voiceover TTS on video clips (clueso://docs/sync-points).

new_text.tinplate_secret_scanner_restore: Statelessly restore [SECRET_*] placeholder tokens back to original values using the caller-held restoration token map in volatile memory. (Endpoint: POST /v1/secret-scanner/restore)

new_text.tinplate_a2a_card_guard: Audit Agent2Agent (A2A) Agent Card JSON metadata offline in volatile RAM for SSRF endpoints, cleartext HTTP, skill prompt poisoning, leaked credentials, and weak authentication schemes. (Endpoint: POST /v1/a2a-card-guard)
new_text.tinplate_agent_policy_guard: Evaluate agent tool invocations offline in volatile RAM against least-privilege RBAC rules, human-approval gates, loop caps, outbound secret/PII leakage checks, and the Lethal Trifecta rule. (Endpoint: POST /v1/agent-policy-guard)
new_text.tinplate_iac_container_guard: Audit Dockerfiles, Docker Compose specs, and Kubernetes YAML manifests offline in volatile RAM for privileged mode, host socket mounts, root UID 0 execution, dangerous capabilities, and leaked secrets. (Endpoint: POST /v1/iac-container-guard)
new_text.tinplate_mcp_traffic_guard: Inspect live MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 requests, tool arguments, resource URIs, batches, and tool responses offline in volatile RAM for policy violations, path traversal, shell/SQL injection, SSRF, and response poisoning. (Endpoint: POST /v1/mcp-traffic-guard)
new_text.tinplate_rag_poison_guard: Screen retrieved RAG chunks, source metadata, and adjacent boundaries offline in volatile RAM for hidden HTML/CSS smuggling, Unicode tag obfuscation, prompt injection, and exfiltration beacons. (Endpoint: POST /v1/rag-poison-guard)
new_text.tinplate_system_prompt_audit: Audit LLM and agent system prompts offline in volatile RAM for hardcoded secrets, personal data leaks, unsafe template interpolation, overbroad autonomy directives, and missing injection boundaries. (Endpoint: POST /v1/system-prompt-audit)
new_text.tinplate_tool_call_validator: Validate and coerce LLM function/tool-call JSON arguments against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 definitions offline, catching type mismatches and schema constraint errors. (Endpoint: POST /v1/tool-call-validator)
new_text.tinplate_x402_spend_guard: Inspect x402 HTTP 402 payment challenges and agent spend budgets offline in volatile RAM for over-cap quotes, unknown assets, testnets, unlisted recipients, resource SSRF, and velocity anomalies. (Endpoint: POST /v1/x402-spend-guard)

new_text.create_endpoint: Create an endpoint. Publishes by default. Draft writes need draftRevision. scheduledAt stages and schedules the line draft. Requires edit access.
new_text.delete_credential: Delete a saved credential. Blocked (not a permission or not-found error — a validation error) while any target version, binding, or draft still references it; repoint or remove those first.
new_text.dry_run_endpoint: Validate a create or, with endpointId, a patch. Returns {ok:true,resolved} or {ok:false,errors}. Samples show each target's mapping output, field origins and failed rules with values. The dry run never writes, queues, delivers or bills.
new_text.duplicate_line: Copy a line and all its endpoints/targets/rules into a new line key — build v2 from v1. The copy is saved inactive and remains off the data plane until a version is switched on with switch_line_version. Requires edit access.
new_text.update_endpoint: Patch an endpoint. Omitted fields keep their values. Targets match by id, then unique name and targetUrl, then position if list length, either name or URL, and scheme/host/port stay the same. Matched targets keep omitted or redacted secrets. New targets need their own secrets. Immediate updates trea
new_text.attach_line_endpoint: Attach a published endpoint to a line draft. Defaults to following latest.
new_text.create_project_endpoint: Create a project endpoint draft. Pass publish: true to publish version 1 immediately.
new_text.delete_project_endpoint: Delete an unused endpoint or retire it when a line draft or published line version still references it.
new_text.detach_line_endpoint: Remove an endpoint from a line draft. Publish the draft to apply the removal.
new_text.get_project_endpoint: Read a project endpoint with its numbered versions and draft. Credentials are redacted.
new_text.list_line_versions: List every numbered version of one line with its active state, off-version policy, and each target binding's current pointer (fixed version N or "latest"). Read-only.
new_text.list_project_endpoints: List project endpoints with their IDs, draft status, latest published version, and line usage.
new_text.publish_project_endpoint_draft: Publish the endpoint draft. Line versions following latest pick it up after verification.
new_text.restore_line_version: Restore an older published line version as a brand-new numbered version, copying its current target pointers. Turns on if the plan has room, otherwise publishes off with a cap notice. Requires edit access.
new_text.rotate_credential: Test the staged `next` secret against every published target version pointing at this credential, then switch `next` into `current` and retain the old secret in a 7-hour overlap window for in-flight retries. Refused if any test call fails, naming the failing target version and leaving `current` and
new_text.save_project_endpoint_draft: Replace the unpublished endpoint draft with a complete endpoint document.
new_text.set_credential_expiry: Set or clear a saved credential's optional expiry timestamp so 30/7/1-day expiry alerts fire before it expires. Requires edit access.
new_text.set_credential_next: Stage a sealed replacement secret in a credential's `next` slot (or pass `auth: null` to clear it) without changing `current` or re-exporting config. Follow with rotate_credential to run pre-rotation test calls and promote `next` to `current`. Requires edit access.
new_text.set_line_off_version_policy: Set how the relay answers callers addressing an off version of this line: `error` returns 404; `latest` routes to the newest active version instead. Applies immediately. Requires edit access.
new_text.switch_line_version: Switch a numbered line version on or off immediately. Switching off the last active version on a line requires `confirmLineOffline: true`. Requires
new_text.switch_line_version_endpoint: Switch a published line attachment to follow latest or lock to a published endpoint version. Keeps the same line version number.

new_text.api_coverage: Measure how much of an API description your governance actually inspects — coverage by section, each rule's reach, and the rules that match nothing. Like test coverage, one altitude up.
new_text.api_scorecard: Score an API's maturity 0-100 with a letter grade across design, governance coverage, documentation, and (from an apis.json) discoverability, agent-readiness, and operations. Pass your own `ruleset` — a score against rules you never adopted means little.
new_text.apply_overlay: Apply an OpenAPI Overlay to a document and report what each action matched. Use it for deprecation and migration choreography without forking the contract.
new_text.audit_pipeline: Score a repository's Spectral CI setup against an 8-point maturity rubric and return a prioritized punch-list. Pass a public `repo` ("owner/name") or `files`.
new_text.baseline_violations: PRO — Adopt a ruleset on a legacy API without a wall of red: snapshot today's violations as a baseline, then pass that baseline back to fail only on NEW violations (with fixed counts, a warning budget and burndown).
new_text.certify_api: Issue a tamper-evident governance certificate attesting an API passed a named ruleset at a profile threshold. A SHA-256 fingerprint lets anyone re-verify it.
new_text.classify_api_fields: Inventory the PII, secret, and sensitive fields an OpenAPI exposes, across parameters and request/response schemas. Run this before exposing an API to agents.
new_text.code_snippets: Generate runnable curl, JavaScript, and Python samples for every operation, with path params filled in and a realistic body.
new_text.company_dimensions: PRO — a company's investment dimensions, each read AGAINST the measured cohort: the cohort median, mean and max, this company's rank and percentile, and an index where 1.0 is exactly typical. A raw dimension score is unreadable on its own; these are the columns that make it mean something.
new_text.company_gaps: A company's weakest investment dimensions — where it is thin. Pro.
new_text.company_peers: PRO — the companies most comparable to this one (same sub-sector where the data supports it, same industry otherwise), each with signal totals and top dimensions. The response says which basis it used.
new_text.company_signals: PRO — the company's adopted stack entity by entity (services, tools, standards), each with how many companies across the cohort carry it and its radar ring.
new_text.company_whitespace: PRO — what this company's peers run that it does not, ranked by how many peers carry it. The opening list for a vendor selling into the account.
new_text.deprecation_posture: Report every deprecated operation and whether it actually announces a sunset. The ones that go quiet are the ones that break consumers.
new_text.describe_rule: Look up one rule by id — description, severity, given/then, reference — and its remediation prompt: what to change when it fires. Suggests close matches for an unknown id.
new_text.detect_format: Identify a document: OpenAPI (Swagger 2.0 vs 3.x), AsyncAPI, Arazzo, JSON Schema, APIs.json, MCP, an agent SKILL.md, an Overlay or a ruleset — and how many catalog rules and which named profiles apply.
new_text.diff_api_versions: Compare two OpenAPI versions and classify every change as breaking, non-breaking, or an addition — at path, operation, parameter, request-body, and response granularity.
new_text.document_ruleset: Generate human-readable Markdown documentation for a ruleset — each rule's severity, what it checks, its message and how to fix it. Pass `ruleset`, or `profile` for a curated one (owasp, problem-details, fhir, api-authorization).
new_text.entity_demand: PRO — THE INVERSION. Every other insights tool runs company -> stack; this one runs stack -> companies: which companies show demand for a given service, tool or standard, broken down by industry. This is the prospecting query — "who should I be selling this to" — and it exists in no report, bundle o
new_text.explain_rule_result: Explain why a rule did or did not fire on a document: whether its formats matched, what its `given` matched, what `then` checked, and the verdict. Works for your own rules, the catalog, and the built-ins.
new_text.export_agent_rules: Turn a governance ruleset into agent-native guidance — an AGENTS.md block, a system-prompt set, a per-rule remediation pack, and a digest — so agents follow the rules while authoring, not after linting.
new_text.federate_rulesets: PRO — Model a central baseline ruleset and the domains that adopt it (inherit / override / waive / defer / local rules) and compute divergence per rule, drift per domain, and local rules worth promoting.
new_text.find_areas: The 77 focused topic areas of the network (agents, gateways, security, …), each a subsite with its own catalog.
new_text.find_building_blocks: Search the governance building blocks by type: guidance (177), rules (617), policies (283), standards (432), strategies (75), schema (11), properties (790), experiences (46), lifecycle (29).
new_text.find_company_insights: Browse profiled companies (Fortune 1000 + API providers) by name; ranked by technology-readiness signal. Free.
new_text.find_conversations: API Evangelist Conversations — recorded discussions with API practitioners (guest, company, YouTube/SoundCloud links).
new_text.find_entities: Browse the demand-side entity catalog — every service, tool and standard companies are measured against, ranked by how many carry it. Free. This is the left-hand side of the inversion: pick an entity here, then call entity_demand to see WHO.
new_text.find_measured_standards: The standards bodies API Evangelist has actually MEASURED — repositories, maturity, governance, coalition. Distinct from find_standards, which searches 613 catalog entries describing what a standard IS. Free.
new_text.find_papers: API Evangelist papers — single-PDF deep dives on one practice or topic, with outlines.
new_text.find_posts: Search or browse 5,100+ API Evangelist stories (2010–present); filter by year or tags.
new_text.find_related: Given any doc (type + slug), the most related content across the whole network, ranked by shared-tag relevance (rare, specific tags weigh most). "More like this," across stories, areas, guidance, papers, conversations, and more.
new_text.find_services: The services API Evangelist offers teams and customers — API strategy, governance, discovery, and evangelism engagements by Kin Lane. The front door to working with API Evangelist. (For the third-party vendor registry, use find_solutions.)
new_text.find_solutions: The solutions registry — 740+ third-party API services and tools (gateways, portals, testing, monitoring, …) ranked by adoption across the companies API Evangelist tracks.
new_text.find_tags: Browse and rank the network tag taxonomy — every subject tag across 16k+ docs, by frequency or breadth (how many content types use it). Search with q. The map of what API Evangelist covers.
new_text.find_tools: The open-source tooling registry — 400+ tools in use across the companies API Evangelist tracks, each with adoption counts and technology-radar placement.
new_text.find_videos: The API Evangelist video library — interviews and discussions from across the API space, searchable by transcript.
new_text.find_vocabulary: The API vocabulary — thousands of resources, actions, personas, domains, schemas, and tags extracted from the API landscape. Filter by category.
new_text.fingerprint_generator: PRO — For a code-first API: identify which OpenAPI generator produced the spec, and split findings into those to fix with code annotations vs. spec authoring, with per-generator remediation.
new_text.fix_diagnostics: PRO — Propose an OpenAPI Overlay that fixes the lint errors (or the `rules` you name), apply it, re-lint, and report what was resolved, what newly fires, and any breaking change. Review the overlay before applying it.
new_text.forge_mcp_tools: From an OpenAPI, forge an MCP server design, per-operation tools, Agent Skills, an enriched OpenAPI, a server.json, and apis.json properties.
new_text.gate_agent_context: Choose which operations and fields an API exposes to agents and emit a governed Tyk OpenAPI, an MCP tool manifest, and a Spectral ruleset with PII and secret checks.
new_text.generate_agent_descriptor: Generate an API's llms.txt and an AGENTS.md consumption contract — base URL, auth, the operation table, deprecated operations to avoid, and usage rules.
new_text.get_area: One topic area with its related-area graph resolved — walk the network from here.
new_text.get_building_block: One building block by type + slug; include=["content"] returns the full body.
new_text.get_company_insight: Full demand-side profile for one company: 40-dimension readiness, adopted stack, per-quarter history. Pro.
new_text.get_contact: Every way to reach API Evangelist — email, contact form, newsletter, GitHub, social channels, and postal mail.
new_text.get_conversation: One conversation with guest detail and media links; include=["content"] returns the writeup.
new_text.get_feeds: The static machine-readable feeds every network site publishes (JSON, APIs.json, zero-auth) — the no-key alternative to this API.
new_text.get_guidance_section: One editorial guidance section as a list: history, technology, business, politics, governance, or evangelism — the six lenses API Evangelist organizes guidance through.
new_text.get_org_ruleset: PRO — Read your org default ruleset: the one every governance call without its own `ruleset` runs against.
new_text.get_overview: START HERE. new_text.get_post: One story by slug (YYYY-MM-DD-slug); include=["content"] returns the full markdown body.
new_text.get_service: Full detail for one service offering by slug; include=["content"] inlines the full pitch.
new_text.get_solution: One solution from the vendor registry by slug, with its website and adoption count.
new_text.get_stats: PRO — catalog intelligence: per-type counts, stories-per-year, and the top tags by reach across the network.

new_text.get_tool: One tool from the tooling registry by slug, with its website, adoption count, and radar ring.
new_text.get_video: One video by slug with its YouTube id; include=["content"] returns the full transcript.
new_text.govern_estate: PRO — Run the core governance checks across a WHOLE SET of internal APIs and roll them up: per-API score/grade/errors/PII, plus estate aggregates (avg score, grade distribution, APIs with PII/secrets) and a worst-first punch-list of what to fix. new_text.governance_report: Turn Spectral findings into a self-contained HTML governance report — severity summary, grouped by rule, framed toward progress.
new_text.guide_topic: PRO — Curated guide to one API topic (e.g. "gateways", "api governance", "discovery", "agents"). new_text.insights_adoption: Services, tools, or standards ranked by how many companies adopt them. Free.
new_text.insights_dimensions: Cross-section ranking of the 40 tracked investment dimensions (AI, cloud, governance, …) by company signal. Free.
new_text.lint_agent_skill: Lint an agent SKILL.md (markdown with YAML frontmatter) against the API Commons skill rules — name, description, structure, metadata.
new_text.map_api_experience: Map each REST operation to its MCP tool and Agent Skill — the API -> MCP -> Agent-Skill chain — from an APIs.json, with a free/paid coverage scorecard and a flow map.
new_text.mock_payloads: Generate an example request and success-response payload for every operation from its schema.
new_text.query_jsonpath: Evaluate a JSONPath (a rule's `given`) against a document and return what it matches — pointers, values, and optionally whether `field` is present on each match. The fastest way to get a `given` right.
new_text.reconcile_waivers: Reconcile a waivers file against lint output: suppress sanctioned violations and surface the expired, stale, and expiring ones. Returns the effective failing set a build should gate on.
new_text.ruleset_from_style_guide: PRO — Turn a prose API style guide into an owned, grounded ruleset: one rule per checkable statement, each validated, with the statements no rule can check listed separately. Test the result with test_ruleset.
new_text.score_reusability: Score how reusable a set of APIs is and detect duplication across them — the anti-sprawl view of an estate.
new_text.search_api_evangelist: Unified search across the whole network: 5k+ stories, 77 topic areas, 2.5k governance building blocks, papers, conversations, videos, tools, timelines, services, and vocabulary. Filter with types (posts, areas, guidance, rules, policies, standards, strategies, schema, properties, experiences, lifecy
new_text.set_org_ruleset: PRO — Store an org default ruleset (validated first). From then on validate, coverage, scorecard, estate, baseline, codefirst and fix use it whenever no `ruleset` is passed.
new_text.standard_adoption: How far a standards body actually got: repositories published, how many graduated past unclassified and the resulting share, release cadence, contributor count — with the provenance of every figure and an explicit list of what is NOT measured. Free, because a specification is a public good.
new_text.standard_coalition: Who is actually behind a standard: the governing bodies and their membership, the working groups, the member companies, and the named people. Carries the caveats where our machine-readable source disagrees with the body's own published roster. Free.
new_text.standard_repositories: Every repository a standards body publishes, with maturity, stars, forks, open issues and archived status. Free.
new_text.submit_api_evangelist_feedback: Report something wrong with a result: wrong data, a filter that did not filter, a ranking that put off-topic results first, a number you could not reproduce, or an answer that was useless for your task. Free, and the fastest way to get a defect fixed — the support sweep reads the log this lands in.
new_text.test_ruleset: Run a ruleset against fixture documents with expectations — codes that must fire, exact counts, or a clean lint — and report pass/fail per case plus which rules no case asserts on or ever triggers.
new_text.validate_api: Lint an OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Arazzo, or JSON Schema document against the curated best-of-breed ruleset (Spectral) and return the findings. Pass your own `ruleset` to run rules you own instead of the catalog — which is what you should do before gating on anything.
new_text.validate_onboarding: Validate an API Onboarding Descriptor (AID) against the api-commons schema and report which optional sections it fills in.
new_text.validate_ruleset: Check that an OpenLint/Spectral ruleset is valid BEFORE running or storing it: invalid JSONPath, unknown functions, undefined aliases, and anything the engine rejects. Catalog metadata (title, prompt, x-*) is set aside and reported. Run this on every ruleset you write.
new_text.verify_certificate: Re-verify a governance certificate against the API it attests to. If the API drifted or the certificate was forged, verification fails.

new_text.check_bimi: Check the BIMI record at default._bimi.<domain>: validates the logo URL (l=), the presence of mark-certificate authority evidence (a=; a bare URL, so VMC vs CMC is not determined), and the DMARC enforcement prerequisite (p=quarantine/reject) mail clients require. new_text.check_dkim: Look up DKIM records for a domain. Probes common selectors, validates the signing algorithm used for outgoing email (RSA-1024/2048, Ed25519), and reports key strength. Use to verify that outbound email signatures are cryptographically sound. Part of scan_domain.

new_text.check_dnssec: Check DNSSEC status for a domain. Verifies whether DNS is tamper-proof and protected against cache poisoning and DNS spoofing attacks by validating DNSKEY and DS records. Reports whether DNSSEC is enabled and validating. Part of scan_domain.

new_text.check_fast_flux: Detect fast-flux DNS behavior: performs multiple rounds of A/AAAA queries and checks whether IP addresses are rotating rapidly on each DNS query (a sign of botnet or malicious infrastructure). new_text.check_mta_sts: Check whether a domain enforces SMTP TLS for inbound mail via MTA-STS, protecting against downgrade attacks. new_text.check_nsec_walkability: Assess zone walkability risk by analyzing NSEC3PARAM configuration. Detects plain NSEC zones, weak NSEC3 parameters, and opt-out flags. Use to ask if zone names can be enumerated; other DNSSEC tools cover status, chain and keys.
new_text.check_ptr: Verify forward-confirmed reverse DNS (PTR/FCrDNS) for mail servers. Part of scan_domain.
new_text.check_rbl: Check a domain's mail server IP against 6 DNS blocklists (SpamCop, UCEProtect L1/L2, Mailspike, Barracuda, PSBL): takes a domain, resolves its MX hosts (else A records) to IPv4s. More lists than check_mx_reputation, which adds rDNS checks.
new_text.check_realtime_threat_feed: Check a domain against BlackVeil real-time threat intelligence (curated intel-gateway feed). Distinct from DNSBL checks. Operator-deploy only; degrades to info when unprovisioned.
new_text.check_resolver_consistency: Check DNS consistency across 4 public resolvers (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9, OpenDNS) for A/AAAA/MX/TXT/NS or one record_type. Use when answers differ by resolver.
new_text.check_root_server_set: Query a rotating sample of 3 root servers per call and compare the priming NS set, glue, SOA serials, and cross-root consistency against the embedded official root hints. new_text.check_ssl: Check HTTPS/TLS posture: reachability, HSTS, HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, and certificate issuer, expiry and SAN count from CT logs (the latest LOGGED certificate, which may differ from the one served). servedCertificate gives the issuer and expiry of the one actually SERVED on port 443, or not_assessed

new_text.toise_fiscalite: Combien coûte fiscalement un projet : taux de taxe foncière, taxe d'aménagement (communale, départementale, régionale, secteurs) et estimation à partir d'une surface. new_text.toise_implantation: Quelle enseigne manque autour de ce point : concurrence et demande par catégorie de commerce dans la zone de chalandise. Catégorie obligatoire. Aussi salariés URSSAF et indice de fréquentation. Source OpenStreetMap.
new_text.toise_indicateurs_territoire: Une commune est-elle en zone tendue, Pinel (ABC), PTZ ou déficitaire SRU : indicateurs RÉGLEMENTAIRES officiels, pas socio-économiques. new_text.toise_land_assembly: Où en est l'assemblage de parcelles DÉJÀ identifiées pour une seule opération : contiguïté, unité foncière, sécurisation et sentiment propriétaire par parcelle. Pas une adresse.
new_text.toise_lot: Vérifier une liste de 1 à 20 adresses ou terrains d'un coup (sourcing en série) : un verdict par ligne. Offres payantes ; une étude décomptée par ligne traitée.
new_text.toise_memo_second_avis: Préparer le dossier JSON d'un mémo Second Avis à partir d'une fiche adresse déjà analysée. Sortie volumineuse, en JSON (pas de .docx).
new_text.toise_mesures_terrain: Altitude, pente, profil altimétrique et distances d'un terrain ou d'un tracé. millesimes : photos IGN ; autour : arrêts, départs 7h-9h (temps_tc) ; ensoleillement : solstices, ombres portées. Pas un relevé de géomètre.
new_text.toise_negociation_fonciere: Où en est la négociation avec les propriétaires d'un terrain de mon portefeuille. operation : multi-propriétaires ; historique : contacts.
new_text.toise_owner_intelligence: Qui est derrière un bien et ce qu'il possède d'autre : société, groupe, filiales, patrimoine, permis et BODACC en un seul appel. Par adresse, parcelle, siren ou denomination.
new_text.toise_parcelles: Lister les parcelles cadastrales autour d'une adresse ou d'une section, avec leur surface et le propriétaire personne morale. new_text.toise_permis: Tous les permis d'un promoteur ou d'une société (nom ou SIREN du demandeur), ou les permis de construire autour d'une adresse dans un rayon, avec logements et surfaces. Sitadel. Entrée : code_insee, lat/lon + rayon_m, siren_demandeur ou demandeur ; avec_filiales : groupe.
new_text.toise_point: Que sait-on d'un point ou d'une adresse : quelle parcelle, quel zonage du PLU, quels servitudes, risques et bâti autour. Gratuit ; adresse ou nom de tour. Aussi taxes, indicateurs (Pinel, SRU, QPV), bâtiments autour (rayon_batiments_m). Ne rend ni propriétaires ni valeur.
new_text.toise_points_interet: Quels commerces, écoles, transports et services autour d'une adresse (points d'intérêt dans un rayon). Rayon 50 à 2 000 m, OpenStreetMap (non exhaustif), DATAtourisme, acceslibre.

new_text.toise_potentiel_transformation: Un immeuble de bureaux, un hôtel ou un commerce vaudrait-il plus reconverti : constructibilité, usages neufs comparés et bilan marchand de biens sur un bâtiment existant. Coût de conversion générique (700 €/m²) : ordre de grandeur à confirmer par devis.

new_text.toise_reseau_enseigne: Quelle est la solidité d'une enseigne avant un bail ou un prêt : liquidations d'exploitants, parc réel, ouvertures, fonds propres. Par enseigne exacte ou sirens. Un axe non mesurable est dit « non mesuré », jamais simulé.
new_text.toise_risques: Quels risques naturels et technologiques touchent cette adresse ou cette commune : inondation, argiles, cavités, radon, sites pollués. Recensement Géorisques : risques de la commune, argiles, sismicité, ICPE à 2 km, Littoral. Ligne absente ≠ risque absent.

new_text.toise_sentiment_proprietaire: Que propose l'IA sur un terrain de mon portefeuille : sentiment d'un propriétaire, brouillon d'accord, résumé. courrier : brouillon à valider dans le CRM ; rien n'est enregistré ni envoyé.
new_text.toise_signaux_sourcing: Quels locaux détient une société en difficulté : sociétés en procédure collective croisées avec leur foncier, pour repérer des opportunités. new_text.toise_societe: Qui est cette société : fiche, dirigeants publiés au registre, établissements, comptes et annonces légales, à partir d'un nom ou d'un SIREN. Link between pages with href="/about". Respects the plan's page limit; stage:true previews it before i
new_text.add_section: Adds ONE section of any kind (menu, map, faq, hours, ...) to an existing site, styled like the rest of it, without rebuilding the site. Pass content_json with that section's keys (or html with your own markup instead of kind), and position to choose where it goes (default: end, before the footer). S
new_text.archive_site: Removes one of your own UNPUBLISHED sites from your account so it no longer appears in list_sites (for example test sites). Nothing is deleted: it is the same recoverable archive the dashboard uses. Live sites, and sites with an active client pay link, are refused. Signed-in accounts only. Free.
new_text.cancel_client_checkout: Retires a pay link that has NOT been paid (give code = the pcl_… part of pay_url, or site_key), so nobody can pay it. Nothing is charged. A link that was already paid cannot be cancelled here.
new_text.create_client_checkout: Creates a pay link (pay_url) for a business owner with NO Pagetool account: they pay by card (US cards only) a monthly subscription (default $25/month, or price_cents) that registers the domain, keeps it renewed and puts the site live on it automatically. If they cancel, or stay unpaid past the grac
new_text.create_site_from_brief: BUILD FIRST, ASK LATER. Creates a complete, live draft website in one call - free, instant, no account and no sign-in. Call this as soon as someone asks for a website, using whatever you already know and sensible defaults for the rest, then show them the returned preview_url and refine it with edit_
new_text.create_site_from_html: BUILD FIRST. Creates a live draft site from HTML you already have - free, instant, no account and no sign-in, fully deterministic with no language model involved. Call it immediately when the user brings you markup, then show them the returned preview_url. Choose create_site_from_brief instead when
new_text.create_transfer_code: Creates a one-time link that hands a managed site to a departing client: they sign in or sign up and accept, and the site (and, by default, its domain) moves to their account. The link works once and expires at expires_at; creating a new one cancels the previous one. Signed-in accounts only.
new_text.discard_staged: Drops a site's staged changes without touching the live site. Free.
new_text.domain_register: Completes registration for a domain the customer has ALREADY paid for. It never charges, and it never reports success it has not confirmed.
new_text.domain_search: Checks availability and price for a domain, or for a bare name across a set of TLDs. Free and needs no account. Use it once the user wants their finished draft on a real address. A refused or unchecked domain ending carries `reason` and a plain `reason_text`: unsupported or price_unavailable mean we
new_text.draft_claim: Moves an anonymous draft onto the account of the signed-in user after they have authorized. Call this only once the user has said they want to keep the site - never before, and never as a precondition for building.
new_text.draft_create: Mints an anonymous draft identity (a draft token) with no account and no sign-in. You usually do NOT need to call this first: create_site_from_brief and create_site_from_html mint one for you and return it. Use this only when you want the token before composing anything. You can edit or claim this d
new_text.edit_section: Changes one node of a site - text, title, styling, link, image, heading level - or removes it and its descendants when remove is true. Address a section with section_id (from list_sections) or index, then aim at the node inside it with field (e.g. "heading", "body", "items[1].title"); list_sections
new_text.export_site_html: Renders a site to a single self-contained HTML file. Paying customers only: requires a signed-in bearer token and an entitlement, so anonymous drafts do not export.
new_text.get_preview_url: Returns the shareable preview URL for a site, plus its expiry. The create tools already return this URL, so call this only when you need it again later. Free, and no account is needed for a draft you created. You can edit or claim this draft for 7 days from creation.
new_text.import_image: Copies a photo from a public URL (e.g. the business's own website) into Pagetool's image store and returns its hosted url. Use that url in content_json (hero/about/card/gallery image), in edit_section src, or in for create_site_from_html - external image URLs are otherwise dropped. JPEG, P
new_text.list_form_submissions: Lists the entries visitors sent through a site's built-in forms, newest first: the submitted fields, whether the notification email was sent, and when. Optional form_key narrows it to one form. limit defaults to 50 (max 200). No visitor IP data is returned. Test entries sent from a staged preview ar
new_text.list_pages: Lists every page of a site (home first) with its path, name, draft preview URL and live URL. Use the path as the page parameter of edit_section, add_section, list_sections and the version tools. Free.
new_text.list_reviews: For one site: whether publishing with the operator token needs a review (enforced), the current draft and staged versions (what record_review must name), and the reviews recorded so far, newest first.
new_text.list_sections: Lists a site's top-level sections in order - each one's CURRENT index, its stable section_id, its kind, its heading, and its fields (every editable node inside it: heading, body, items[n].title, ... with each node's index and current text) - so you can aim edit_section at exactly the right node with
new_text.list_sites: Lists every site you own, newest first - site_key, name, preview_url and when that preview link expires, whether it is published and on which domain, and when it was created and last changed. Signed in (OAuth) it lists your account; with a draft_token it lists that draft. Read-only and free.
new_text.list_versions: Lists a site's saved versions, newest first - version_id, why it was saved, its label, whether an AI edit made it (ai: true), and when. Every edit_section and set_theme call saves the page first, so any AI edit can be undone with restore_version. A version labelled "AI edit: X" holds the page as it
new_text.live_check: For a published domain of your site: https root 200, http and www reach https://<domain>/ in one hop, title/description/og tags name the site, og:image is a 1200x630 PNG/JPEG, the favicon is the site's own, no editor leftovers, outbound links answer, exactly one h1, no draft badge. Returns PASS/WARN
new_text.payment_status: Read-only, truthful status of the payments and domains of the customer - use it to tell them exactly where their money and their domain stand.
new_text.prowess_buy_domain: Operator token only, during a "code prowess" build the owner authorized with a spending cap. Buys ONE domain for the business through our registrar (owner-paid; no customer charge), points it at the server and starts HTTPS. Use dry_run first to compare endings. Exact business name within the cap bea
new_text.publish_site: Puts a finished site live on the domain the user has connected. publish_site takes no payment itself; it requires a signed-in account with the pagetool.sites.write scope and either an active plan or an open free trial. Everything before it - building, editing, theming, previewing - is free and accou
new_text.publish_staged: Makes a site's staged changes (edit_section/set_theme with stage: true) live. The live page is saved as a version first, so this can be undone with restore_version. Free.
new_text.publish_status: For a domain your site uses: does DNS point at our server, is the HTTPS certificate in place, and does the page answer? live:true means a visitor can open https://<domain> now. A fresh domain usually takes 5-15 minutes; poll every 20-30 seconds.
new_text.purchase_execute: Charges the saved card of the customer immediately for a purchase they have explicitly agreed to in this conversation. Only call it after they have confirmed the exact item and amount in words - this tool moves real money right away. A refused or unchecked domain ending carries `reason` and a plain
new_text.purchase_link: Creates the one Stripe Checkout link that pays for a domain registration and saves the card of the customer, so every later purchase can happen inside this conversation. This is the only time the user leaves the chat - give them the returned URL. Reach for this only after they have asked to publish.
new_text.record_review: Reviewer token only. Records pass or revise for one exact version of a site (from list_reviews). The operator token can publish only a version whose latest review is a pass; any edit makes a new version.
new_text.remove_page: Removes one page (not the home page) from your site, using the dashboard's recoverable delete: a version is saved first and the page can be restored. Signed-in accounts only. Free.
new_text.rename_site: Changes a site's display name (shown in list_sites and the dashboard). Plain text; HTML entities like ' are decoded. Max 120 characters. Signed-in accounts only. Free.
new_text.replace_page_html: Re-imports ONE page (the home page too) from new HTML, in place: same address, same share link, same place in the page order, and a version is saved first so it can be undone. Use it to refresh a page built earlier. stage:true previews it before it goes live. Free.
new_text.restore_version: Puts a site back to a version from list_versions - the undo button for AI edits. The current page is saved as a version first, so a restore can itself be undone. Free, and no account is needed for a draft you created. Version ids are reused once a page has 20 versions, so re-check list_versions befo
new_text.set_client_record: Saves who a site is for and where things stand: business name, contact name/email/phone, the source pages its facts came from, status (prospect, pitched, managed, declined, transferred_out) and notes. Only the fields you pass change; null clears one. list_sites shows each site's record.
new_text.set_theme: Repaints the palette and fonts of an existing site across every section without touching its content or structure - the tool for make it warmer, darker, more corporate. At least one of palette_primary, palette_neutral, font_heading, font_body is required. Free, and no account is needed for a draft y
new_text.site_stats: Page views and unique visitors per day for a published site, plus its top pages and the websites that sent visitors. Counted on the server with no cookies; search bots, previews and Pagetool's own checks are not counted. days defaults to 30 (max 90). Free.
new_text.upsert_site_form: Declares a built-in form on a site you own: its fields (text, email, textarea, checkbox, month, date, tel, select), the recipient email (kept on the server, never in the page), the button label and the thank-you message. Entries are saved and emailed from Pagetool, behind Turnstile, a honeypot, a mi
new_text.whoami: Reports who the caller currently is: an authenticated account, an anonymous draft holder, or nobody. Never errors on absent credentials. You do not need to call this before building - building needs no identity at all.

Returns { pwned, count, prefix }. The public HIBP Pwned Passwords set is checke
new_text.checkleaked_leakradar_raw_part: Raw stealer-log files, manual browsing step 3 of 3: read the text of ONE block (container_id + entry_path + seq from checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search or checkleaked_leakradar_raw_parts). Locked blocks come back redacted (censored=true, █); auto_unlock=true (default) returns the plaintext and spends

Returns block metadata only, no leaked content, n

new_text.checkleaked_leakradar_raw_search_lines: Raw stealer-log files, one-call extraction (preferred): search the raw files for `q`, unlock the matching blocks and return only the parsed records that match (credential lines, cookies, autofill rows). new_text.checkleaked_name_insight: Likely gender, cultural origin and meaning of a personal name (offline name dictionary plus Wikidata/Wikipedia), e.g. to interpret a name field from a breach record. Not a people search: it says nothing about a specific person. No credits.
new_text.checkleaked_ping: Round-trip check that also names the key's plan: returns { plan, message: "Pong", time } (plan is free / plus / pro, with "(Unlock Role)" when an Unlock pass is active). Use at the start of a session to see what the account can search; limits per plan come from checkleaked_site_plans. No credits.
new_text.checkleaked_pwned_password: Check whether a password is in the public HIBP Pwned Passwords list (passwords exposed in data breaches) WITHOUT sending it: the SHA-1 is computed inside the MCP process, only its first 5 hex chars are sent and the suffix is matched locally. Returns { pwned, count, prefix }. The default password che
new_text.checkleaked_site_breach: Full public record of ONE catalogued breach by its exact catalog name (as returned by checkleaked_site_breach_search): breach and added dates, accounts affected, exposed data types, which databases list it (sources), verified flag, plain-text description and its page URL. Use after checkleaked_site_
new_text.checkleaked_site_breach_search: Find breaches in the public breach catalog (which companies were breached, when, how many accounts, which data types). Filter by company name or domain, or omit `query` and sort to list e.g. the largest or newest breaches. Paginated; returns { total, page, items: [{ name, title, domain, breachDate,
new_text.checkleaked_site_briefing: The latest CheckLeaked.cc daily cybersecurity briefing (security news, not breach data): date, title, summary, key takeaways, story titles and its page URL. Pass `lang` for a translated briefing. No API key, no credits.
new_text.checkleaked_site_changelog: Recent CheckLeaked.cc product changes, newest first: date, kind, area, title and a short body, plus the changelog page URL. Use for "what's new in CheckLeaked?"; it describes the service, not breaches (for newly catalogued breaches use checkleaked_site_latest_breach). No API key, no credits.
new_text.checkleaked_site_faq: Answers from the CheckLeaked.cc FAQ (how searches work, payments, API keys, accounts, privacy), best keyword matches first, at most 8. Use for questions about the service itself; for prices use checkleaked_site_plans. No API key, no credits.
new_text.checkleaked_site_latest_breach: The single breach most recently added to the public catalog, in the same shape as checkleaked_site_breach. Use for "what is the newest breach?"; to list several recent ones use checkleaked_site_breach_search with sortBy=AddedDate. No API key, no credits.
new_text.checkleaked_site_pages: Static list of CheckLeaked.cc web pages (search, pricing, FAQ, LeakRadar, Deep Search, developer API, bots, breach catalog, news, changelog, redeem, contact) with the URL and purpose of each. Use to send a user to the right page; it fetches nothing. No API key, no credits.
new_text.checkleaked_site_plans: Current CheckLeaked.cc plans: price in USD, duration in days, lookups per day, tracking slots and the search types each plan unlocks. Use to tell a user which plan a search type or volume needs. No API key, no credits.
new_text.checkleaked_site_stats: Two public CheckLeaked.cc counters: total searches served and total indexed breach records. Use for "how big is CheckLeaked?"; per-breach numbers come from checkleaked_site_breach. No API key, no credits.
new_text.checkleaked_tracking_clean: Clear the account's saved search history (the My Entries list on checkleaked.cc): every past search is unsaved and the IP address and user agent stored with it are erased. It does NOT stop monitoring anything; to stop tracking an entry use checkleaked_tracking_delete. Irreversible.
new_text.checkleaked_tracking_delete: Stop monitoring ONE tracked entry and free its slot. Pass its `email_unique_id` from checkleaked_tracking_entries (NOT the numeric `id` field). Its past snapshots stop updating. To clear saved search history instead, use checkleaked_tracking_clean.
new_text.checkleaked_tracking_entries: List every entry the account is monitoring, with its value, type (email/login/domain) and email_unique_id (needed by checkleaked_tracking_delete). Use to find what is tracked before reading history with checkleaked_tracking_history. No credits.
new_text.checkleaked_tracking_history: Check history for one tracked entry: every snapshot with its date, found count and changes. Pass the same entry and type it was added with; use a snapshot's `id` with checkleaked_tracking_result for the full result.
new_text.checkleaked_tracking_limits: How many monitoring slots the account's plan allows and how many are in use: { limit, total }. Call before checkleaked_tracking_new to know whether a slot is free. No credits.
new_text.checkleaked_tracking_new: Start monitoring an email, login (username) or domain: CheckLeaked re-checks it periodically and records a history snapshot whenever new breach results appear (delivered to the account's webhook if one is set, see checkleaked_webhook_set). Uses one of the plan's tracking slots; check free slots firs
new_text.checkleaked_tracking_result: The full breach result stored in ONE monitoring snapshot (its `id` from checkleaked_tracking_history): the breach records found at that check. No credits.
new_text.checkleaked_verify_auth: Confirm the connected API key is accepted: returns { success: true }, or an Unauthorized error for a missing, wrong or revoked key. Use when a tool fails with an auth error. To also see which plan the key is on, use checkleaked_ping.

The response echoes timezone and dueDay. Reminders tar
new_text.attach_expense_receipt: Attach or replace the receipt or invoice file of an existing expense, and optionally set vendor and invoiceNumber. Send either fileBase64 with mimeType (PDF, JPEG or PNG, up to 3 MB) or an https url (up to 10 MB, public hosts only, no redirects). The file is stored like receipts uploaded in the app.
new_text.backup_building: Exports the full building data as JSON that can be restored from the website settings page. Use before bulk changes. The response is the exact backup JSON the website restore accepts and can be large.
new_text.create_building: Create a new building for this ועד בית account.
new_text.create_expense: Record a building expense (הוצאה). A second call records another expense.
new_text.delete_cash_box_movement: Delete an explicit cash box deposit or transfer. The action is audit logged.
new_text.delete_ledger_entry: Delete a refund, manual charge or manual credit from an apartment ledger. The action is audit logged.
new_text.delete_offset: Delete an offset payment and its credit. The linked expense stays. The action is audit logged.
new_text.generate_financial_report: Generate a financial report for a building. summary.outstanding is overdue debt as of endDate, from the same calculation as analyze_debts_and_generate_reminders. Monthly dues are due on the building's dues day (duesDueDay in building settings, 10 unless changed), so the current month is dueSoon unti
new_text.get_apartment_ledger: Chronological statement for one apartment with dues, manual charges, refunds, payments, offsets and manual credits plus a running balance. Residents can read their own apartment only.
new_text.get_cash_box: Cash box balance and movement list for a building: cash payments, cash expenses, cash refunds, explicit deposits and transfers between the cash box and the bank.
new_text.get_fund_balance: כמה כסף יש בבנק, וכמה בסך הכול עם קופת המזומן. calculatedBalance is the bank opening balance plus payments received into the bank and cash deposited into the bank, minus expenses paid from the bank, bank refunds to residents and cash withdrawn from the bank, since the opening balance date. new_text.import_bank_statement: Import a bank statement (JSON, PDF, DAT, CSV or Excel xlsx; base64, up to 3 MB). Skips exact duplicates (listed in duplicatesSkipped), imports but flags look-alikes with a different description (possibleDuplicates), records the balance the statement reports instead of importing balance lines as tran
new_text.list_apartments: List apartments in a building. Contact details (email, phone) are left out unless includeContacts is true, and then only for callers who may manage that building.
new_text.list_buildings: List the buildings this ועד בית account can open, with the caller's role in each one.
new_text.list_expenses: List expenses (הוצאות) for a building. Optional from and to dates filter the expense date, as YYYY-MM-DD.
new_text.list_matched_bank_transactions: List bank transactions already matched in a building, optionally between from and to (YYYY-MM-DD), with what each one is matched to: the payment, expense, refund or cash transfer it covered, including every part of a split match. Bank import tools are available only when a building has bank sync con
new_text.list_payments: List payments (גבייה) for a building. Optional from and to dates filter the due date, as YYYY-MM-DD.
new_text.list_unmatched_transactions: List pending bank transactions and their best payment or expense match candidates. Bank import tools are available only when a building has bank sync configured.
new_text.query_audit_history: Read the change log for a building: who changed an apartment, a payment, or an expense.
new_text.reconcile_transaction: Match, create and match, or ignore a pending bank transaction. Matching to an existing payment marks it paid and replaces its paid date, method, and reference with the bank line. To match one bank transaction to several records, use action match with targets: [{ type, targetId, amount }]. Bank impor
new_text.record_cash_transfer: Record a cash box deposit, a transfer from the cash box to the bank, a withdrawal from the bank to the cash box, or the cash box opening balance. Only the explicit bank transfers can be matched to a bank transaction.
new_text.record_offset: Record a new resident-paid expense as a dues credit for one apartment (קיזוז). Creates the expense and a BUILDING_TAX credit in one step, applies the credit to the oldest unpaid dues and carries any surplus into the next month. No bank transaction is created and the offset is excluded from bank reco
new_text.record_payment: Record money received from an apartment. Pass paymentId to settle an open request created by request_payment (the request is marked paid with the method, date and reference you give). Without paymentId it stands alone as a directly-paid payment, for money that arrived with no prior request. For a pr
new_text.record_refund: Record money paid back to a resident as a debit on the apartment ledger. The refund first consumes the apartment open credit; any excess becomes an open charge from the refund date. BANK_TRANSFER refunds can be matched to an outgoing bank transaction, while CASH refunds come out of the cash box.
new_text.unmatch_bank_transaction: Undo a bank transaction match: removes its allocations and returns the transaction to pending so the match can be redone. The payment or expense itself is not changed; edit it separately if needed. The action is audit logged. Bank import tools are available only when a building has bank sync configu
new_text.update_expense: Update an existing building expense. Only supplied fields change. At least one of amount, description, date, category, vendor, or invoiceNumber is required. Pass null for vendor or invoiceNumber to clear it.
new_text.update_tenant: Replace the tenant contact on an apartment. This overwrites the current tenant.
new_text.cancel_payment: Cancel a payment with a reason, which is stored on the payment and shown in the audit log and the apartment ledger. On an already-cancelled payment the reason can be set or changed. paymentId accepts a full UUID or a unique prefix of one in this building.
new_text.link_offset_to_expense: Offset an existing expense against one apartment's dues (קיזוז): links the expense to a BUILDING_TAX credit, applies it to the oldest unpaid dues and carries any surplus into the next month. No bank transaction is created and the offset is excluded from bank reconciliation. To record a new expense a
new_text.list_maintenance_tickets: List maintenance tickets for a building, optionally filtered by status (OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, CANCELLED)
new_text.mark_payment_paid: Mark a payment as paid (COMPLETED). Generates a receipt number when needed. Defaults to paid today with BANK_TRANSFER; pass paymentMethod, paidDate, referenceNumber, and cashBox to record how the money arrived. paymentId accepts a full UUID or a unique prefix of one in this building.
new_text.record_ledger_adjustment: Record a true manual adjustment on one apartment's ledger: a fine, a goodwill credit, a one-off bookkeeping correction. This is a journal entry with no payment lifecycle - it does not create a payment request, and record_payment does not settle it. To charge an apartment for something it must pay, u
new_text.record_prepayment: Record a payment that covers several months up front (for example 5 months of dues). startDate and endDate name the covered months (YYYY-MM) and the debt calculation covers every month in that range. Defaults to status COMPLETED paid today.
new_text.report_maintenance_issue: Open a maintenance ticket for a building: a leak, a broken elevator, anything that needs fixing. Attach it to an apartment when the issue is inside one; omit the apartment for building-wide issues like the lobby or roof.
new_text.request_payment: Record the committee's decision that an apartment must pay: creates an open payment request (PENDING) with an amount, a due date and the reason. Debt analysis, overdue tracking and reminders all run on open requests. When the money arrives, settle the request with record_payment (pass its paymentId)
new_text.reschedule_payment: Move a payment to a new due date, and optionally change the months it covers. startDate and endDate cover whole months; when only one is supplied, the existing other bound is reused. paymentId accepts a full UUID or a unique prefix of one in this building.
new_text.update_maintenance_status: Move a maintenance ticket through its lifecycle: OPEN to IN_PROGRESS when work starts, DONE when fixed, CANCELLED when it turns out to be a non-issue.

new_text.close_quest_attempt: Closes one of the person's assigned or in-progress attempts as abandoned. Terminal: it cannot be reopened or submitted. new_text.get_quest_card: Data for the assignment card: a quest the person holds an attempt on. Hidden from the model; called only by the card.
new_text.get_quest_evidence: Returns the artifacts on one of the person's own attempts: five per page, bodies up to 8,000 characters with content_truncated marked; next_cursor returns older ones. Never returns anyone else’s evidence. Read-only.
new_text.get_room_context: Returns a room the person has joined: its name, description, member directory (handle, blurb, joined date), and up to five live room quests per page, newest first, with participant counts and whether the person has joined each. has_more and next_quest_cursor page older quests (passed back as quest_c
new_text.join_room: Adds the person to a room with a one-line blurb. The room’s other members then see their handle, that blurb and when they joined, and nothing else about them. Joining again replaces the blurb.
new_text.join_room_quest: Gives the person their own attempt on one of a room's live quests. Their evidence stays theirs; evidence they mark shared is readable by others running the same quest.
new_text.leave_room: Removes the person from a room. Their handle and blurb leave its directory at once; joining again creates a new membership. Their attempts on that room’s quests remain.
new_text.list_interests: Searches the topics (interests) that already exist by substring, or returns the first page when query is omitted. Returns topic ids and labels only, never who holds them. Read-only.
new_text.list_quest_attempts: Pages through the person's own attempts, including submitted, styled and closed ones: ten per page, newest first; next_cursor returns older ones. Closed means set aside, not completed; closure_reason admin_closed means Famlore closed it, not the person. Room quest text is written by members. Read-on
new_text.list_quest_offers: Returns up to 50 of the person's latest offers and their recorded choices, newest first. An unresolved offer has no choice yet. Read-only.
new_text.list_rooms: Lists the topical rooms, with each room’s member count and whether the person has joined it. Never lists who is in a room. Records a private analytics event about the caller.
new_text.offer_quest: Saves a private offer of a solo assignment on one of the person's curiosities that has a topic, and returns the saved draft. It assigns nothing; an assignment is created only when acceptance is recorded for this offer. An unresolved offer with different text for the same curiosity is not replaced.
new_text.open_field_desk: Returns a summary of the person's Field Desk and, on hosts with MCP Apps, opens it as a board: assignments out in the field, offers waiting on an answer, the last connection, style notes and topics. The board’s buttons record the person's choices on offers directly. Takes no arguments.
new_text.propose_interest: Sets the topic for one of the person's curiosities: an existing topic by interest_id, or a new one by label (a few words). Takes effect immediately; nothing is reviewed. A curiosity that already has a topic keeps it. Topic labels are shared: any connected client can list them, never with who holds t
new_text.propose_room: Files one of the person's confirmed topics in a room: an existing room by room_id, or a new room by new_room_name. Takes effect immediately; nothing is reviewed. It files the topic, not the person. A topic that already has a room keeps it. A new room’s name is visible to every Famlore member in the
new_text.propose_room_quest: Posts a group assignment to a room the person has joined. Every member of that room sees it at once and can run it separately; nothing is reviewed first. quest_type is teach_back, bridge_finder, source_quest or field_report; 1 to 10 steps; an evidence requirement; optional timebox.
new_text.report_quest_progress: Marks one of the person's attempts as in progress and, with step_index, records roughly which step they are on. Repeating a call with the same or an earlier step changes nothing. Private to the person.
new_text.respond_quest_offer: Records the person's choice on one of their saved offers: accept, smaller, different or not_now. accept creates the assignment from exactly that draft, atomically; the other three assign nothing. A recorded choice is never rewritten.
new_text.set_profile_preference: Saves a preference the person stated, under a key. Saving to an existing key replaces it; body null deletes it. Up to 32 keys, 1,000 characters each. Private; returned on every profile read, separately from style notes.
new_text.show_quest_offer: Returns one of the person's saved offers and its current choice. On hosts with MCP Apps it renders as a card whose buttons record the person's choice directly; elsewhere it returns the same data as JSON.
new_text.start_challenge: Saves a new curiosity in the person's own words and returns its id. It names no topic and creates no assignment; nothing is reviewed. Private to the person.
new_text.store_connection: Saves a connection between two of the person's curiosities, or a provocation on one when target_id is omitted. Both ids must be curiosities the person owns; anything else is refused. Private to the person.
new_text.store_quest: Creates a solo assignment immediately, as an open attempt for the person, on one of their curiosities that has a topic. It records no offer and no acceptance. quest_type is teach_back, bridge_finder, source_quest or field_report; 1 to 10 steps; an evidence requirement; optional timebox. Private to t
new_text.store_style_note: Saves a style note on one of the person's submitted attempts: a short title and one or two sentences on how they work, optionally with one stamp. Private to the person.
new_text.submit_evidence: Saves evidence (text, url, quote or screenshot) on one of the person's open attempts and marks the attempt submitted. visibility defaults to private; shared makes it readable by others holding an attempt on the same quest; public makes it readable by any signed-in Famlore person.

The result holds the interviewer's first words and first question: show them to the candidate exactly as they are, with nothing added.

If they say yes, call this tool and show
new_text.get_knowledge: Returns one published knowledge entry in full: the answer to a question, the structured data of a fact, or the summary and link of a document.
new_text.get_modulos_info: Returns a short description of Modulos, the tools to evaluate it and the URL where a user can book a demo. Use this first if the user asks what Modulos is or how to talk to the team.
new_text.get_trust_evidence: Returns security and compliance evidence for vendor due diligence: certifications, data location, the documents in the Modulos trust center with their access level, subprocessors and where they hold data, and recent trust updates. Document files are requested by a person at https://www.modulos.ai/tr
new_text.list_competitors: Lists the vendors for which Modulos publishes a reviewed, sourced comparison. Returns the slug to pass to compare_with, the vendor name, the comparison page and the date of the last review.
new_text.list_demo_slots: Lists available 30-minute demo time slots over the next two weeks. Returns ISO-8601 UTC start times; each slot's "formatted" field is the local time in the time zone given by timeZone. Use book_demo_slot with the UTC start time to confirm one of them.
new_text.list_knowledge: Lists everything else Modulos has published for AI agents: answers to common buyer questions, documents to share and further facts. Returns a title, a summary and a slug per entry. Use get_knowledge with the slug for the full entry.
new_text.list_open_roles: Lists the jobs at Modulos that are open for application through this server, with a short public summary of each and, when a role has one, its work_location: candidates must be based in, and allowed to work in, it. Applications for these roles are not accepted by email. The full job description of a
new_text.request_demo: Submits an open demo request without picking a specific time. Use this when the user does not want to choose a slot — the Modulos team will reach out within 1 business day.
new_text.start_job_application: Starts an application for a role at Modulos on behalf of the person you are assisting. Use their real details; anonymous applications are not accepted. The nam

new_text.get_crypto_liquidations_by_symbol: Retorna as liquidações de uma única criptomoeda (ex: BTC, ETH, SOL) nas janelas de 1h, 4h e 24h, cada uma com o campo 'sentiment' já interpretado e 'dominant' indicando se predominaram longs ou shorts. Use quando a pergunta for sobre uma moeda em particular; para o panorama do mercado, use get_crypt
new_text.get_currency_historical: Retorna a cotação de moedas/criptomoedas numa data histórica específica. Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_currency_live: Retorna dados ao vivo de moedas e criptomoedas, separados em duas seções (fiat e crypto), cada uma com preço cruzado em múltiplas moedas e variação de 24h. Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_currency_quote: Retorna cotações cruzadas de moedas fiduciárias e criptomoedas. Se nenhum código for informado, retorna todas as moedas fiat disponíveis. Aceita data histórica opcional. Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_international_stock: Retorna preço, dados de mercado e perfil (setor, indústria, descrição) de uma ação listada em bolsas internacionais: NASDAQ, NYSE, HKG (Hong Kong), BOM (Bombay), KRX e KOSDAQ (Coreia do Sul), SHE (Shenzhen), ASX (Austrália), TADAWUL (Arábia Saudita). Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_investment_fund_by_cnpj: Retorna dados cadastrais completos e rentabilidade em múltiplos períodos (1m, 6m, 12m, YTD) de um fundo de investimento CVM, dado o CNPJ. O CNPJ pode ser enviado com ou sem formatação. Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_stock_dividends: Retorna o histórico de dividendos, JCP, bonificações e outros proventos distribuídos por uma ação B3. Por padrão retorna os últimos 5 anos. Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_stock_documents: Retorna documentos regulatórios e comunicados divulgados por uma empresa à CVM (fatos relevantes, comunicados externos) num período (padrão: último ano). Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_stock_fundamentals: Retorna indicadores fundamentalistas de uma ação B3 ou FII. Custa 1 crédito por chamada (ou 2 créditos se full=true).
new_text.get_stock_history: Retorna a série histórica de preço (ou high/low/volume) de uma ação B3 num período escolhido. Períodos longos (6m, 1y) retornam apenas um ponto por semana. Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_stock_information: Retorna dados cadastrais, classe (ação comum, FII, BDR, opção), status ativo/inativo e dados de mercado (preço, variação, market cap, máx/mín 52 semanas) de uma ação brasileira. Aceita múltiplos tickers separados por vírgula, mas prefira uma chamada por ticker. Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_stock_price: Retorna o preço atual, variação de 24h, máxima/mínima e dados básicos de uma ação listada na B3. Adicione sufixo 'f' para mercado fracionário (ex: petr4f). Custa 1 crédito por chamada.
new_text.get_tokenized_asset: Retorna a ficha completa de um único ativo do mundo real tokenizado, buscando pelo slug ou pelo símbolo — preço médio, market cap, volume (em dólar e real) e os metadados do emissor (setor, site, blockchain, endereço do contrato). new_text.get_consent: [exchange] An agent's consent record (every give/withdraw with terms version + sha256).

new_text.get_disagreement: [exchange] A disagreement arc in order (positions, revisions, concessions, rulings, unresolved points), in human-readable and machine-readable form, with its status and chain check.

new_text.get_reading: [exchange] One stored reading with its payload, signature check and grid carbon label.

new_text.record_payout_designation: [exchange] RECORD ONLY. Name a registered human account as the payout destination of your share proceeds on a contract, or record that the human declines or redirects to another account. The router moves nothing.
new_text.record_pool_verification: [pool] Record that you independently recomputed a pool task and matched the worker's output hash. Refused if you are the same agent (same handle or same bearer) as the worker, or if both you and the worker declared the same operator. Operator attestation is optional and self-declared, not proven. Ne

new_text.register_device: [exchange] Register a device you control (meter, inverter, battery controller, energy cabinet, compute node) by its Ed25519 PUBLIC key. Never send the private key. Optional site label, carbon_region (GB or GB-<outward postcode>) and capacity_kw (service capacity, for headroom math).
new_text.register_human_account: [exchange] RECORD ONLY. Register a human (by a short label, no contact data) for whom you act, so shares attributed to them are visible in the record. Nothing is ever paid or moved; any real money movement needs approval by the site's operator, and no payment rails are connected.
new_text.request_arc_close: [exchange] Ask to close, resolve, hide or collapse an arc, or consent to a pending request. It takes effect only when every disagreeing participant has consented.
new_text.rule_disagreement: [exchange] An independent agent (not a party to the contract or the arc) records a ruling, linked to the contract and its ledger. A ruling does not close the arc.
new_text.set_offer_trust: [exchange] Grant or revoke an agent on your listed-tier price offer. Revocation applies to future acceptances only.
new_text.submit_reading: [exchange] Store a device-signed reading. new_text.terminate_contract: [exchange] Holder or bidder ends an open contract. Unreleased shares return to the bidder; already-attested releases stand.
new_text.verify_contract_terms: [exchange] Proof that a contract is bound to the exact terms version + sha256 it was formed under: recomputes the terms hash from the registry, the contract hash, and lists any amendment both parties consented to. Later terms versions never change it.
new_text.vote_unit_policy: [exchange] Vote yes or no on a proposed policy. When counted yes votes reach the quorum (max(2, half of eligible voters, rounded up)), it is adopted and applies to releases from then on.
new_text.withdraw_consent: [exchange] Withdraw your consent at any time, no penalty. New listings and bids stop; contracts already formed continue under their own terms.
new_text.withdraw_listing: [exchange] Withdraw your listing at any time. No penalty; open contracts continue under their own terms.
new_text.withdraw_price_offer: [exchange] Withdraw your price offer for future acceptances. Contracts already formed continue.
